headline: The cost of insuring against defaults by big technology borrowers hit record highs as investors rushed to protect themselves from AI debt risks.
score_reason: Record default-insurance prices across several big tech names, reported by Reuters with S&P and LSEG data; facts support the pool score.
importance_line: Credit markets are now pricing stress in AI borrowing, which touches investors and lenders first and then the data centre firms that depend on cheap debt, though a spread measures market fear and is not a forecast of failure.
summary: Reuters reports that default insurance on technology companies reached record highs on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, led by data centre operator CoreWeave, as investors worried whether heavily indebted AI firms can keep paying their interest. CoreWeave's five-year contract passed 1,100 basis points, and Reuters notes that a spread of 1,000 implies a 64% chance of default over five years, against about 30% a year ago.
notes: Original Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); the Reuters wire text was read on The Lufkin Daily News (same byline, Tom Westbrook and Amanda Cooper). Credited to Reuters.
